subject: DR proofpoints & SLA exception request: forced-failover evidence and timeline
messages:
From: Ravi Shah <ravi.shah@brightwell.health>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: REQ: DR proofpoints + temporary SLA ask

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the SIG follow-up yesterday. As part of our procurement checklist we need a concise set of evidence items for your business continuity posture to share with our internal security and procurement teams. Specific asks:

- Confirm technical RTO and RPO targets (per region) for hosted inference and backend control plane.
- Details on backup frequency, retention, and restore verification cadence.
- Cross-region failover architecture and whether you perform forced-failover drills (and frequency).
- Last successful full failover rehearsal and a short summary of results.
- Any known SLA carve-outs or exceptions we should be aware of (esp during major upgrades/migrations).

We also have a calendar constraint: our security ops team needs the evidence by EOD Friday (4/23). One more note — we are requesting a temporary SLA exception to allow a 2-hour planned maintenance window during our onboarding migration; please indicate whether Redwood can provide that window without impacting contractual RTOs.

Can you send the materials and any artifacts (runbook pages, snapshots of backup configs, test logs) and confirm if you can accommodate the 2-hour window?

Regards,
Ravi Shah
Senior SRE, BrightWell Health
ravi.shah@brightwell.health
[BrightWell procurement request #BW-1879]
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Ravi Shah <ravi.shah@brightwell.health>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: REQ: DR proofpoints + temporary SLA ask

Ravi — thanks for the clear list. Below is a compact summary and attached artifacts; detailed playbook and logs are in the Drive link. If you need additional screenshots or signed attestations we can provide them.

Summary (Hosted API / control plane):
- RTO: 60 minutes (target) for critical inference endpoints in primary region; 180 minutes for non-critical control-plane services during cold-start scenarios.
- RPO: 15 minutes for producer-facing token stores and inference session state; 1 hour for aggregated analytics/metrics.
- Backups: incremental replication every 15 minutes for session/state (KV), daily full snapshot for model/metadata. Retention: 90 days standard; 1-year archival available on request.
- Restore verification: weekly restore-to-staging for critical datasets; monthly full restore drill for primary DBs.
- Cross-region failover: active-passive async replication (primary US-West -> secondary US-East). Failover is orchestrated via our control plane with automated health checks and DNS switchover.
- Forced-failover drills: quarterly for staging; annual full-run for production (last production full-run: 2026-11-03).
- SLA exceptions: We can support a 2-hour planned maintenance window for onboarding migration with SLA crediting if coordinated 7 days in advance; exceptions during emergency upgrades may impact RTO guarantees (we will flag in advance).

Attachments included: dr_playbook_v3.pdf (runbook excerpts), rto_rpo_table.csv (per-service targets), backup_policy_screenshot.png (console snapshot). Drive link has the full playbook and run logs.

Planned next steps: Marcus will propose a forced-failover test slot and Laura will confirm whether procurement/legal need an SLA amendment for the temporary window.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Manager, Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference
